headline: Myths About Domestic Violence Charges in California

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
When you're accused of domestic violence, there's a lot of misinformation out there that can add to an already stressful situation. Let's clear up some common myths about these charges in California, because knowing the facts can truly impact your defense.

Myth: The alleged victim can just drop the charges if they want to. Fact: Once charges are filed by the prosecutor's office, the decision to proceed rests solely with the state, not the alleged victim. Even if the victim recants or doesn't want to press charges, the prosecution can, and often will, continue the case.

Myth: It's only domestic violence if there's physical injury. Fact: Not true. Domestic violence laws in California cover a wide range of behaviors, including emotional abuse, threats, harassment, and even disturbing the peace within a domestic relationship. You don't need to leave a physical mark for charges to be filed.

Myth: You'll automatically go to jail if arrested for domestic violence. Fact: While an arrest often leads to detention, it doesn't automatically mean a conviction or jail time. An experienced defense lawyer can often argue for bail, release on your own recognizance, or work towards an outcome that avoids incarceration, depending on the specifics of your case.

Myth: A temporary restraining order isn't a big deal. Fact: A temporary restraining order (TRO) can have significant immediate impacts, including forcing you out of your home and restricting contact with family. Violating a TRO can lead to new criminal charges. It's absolutely a big deal and requires serious attention and legal counsel.

Myth: Only married couples can be involved in domestic violence cases. Fact: California's domestic violence laws apply to a broad range of relationships, including spouses, cohabiting partners, dating partners, former spouses or partners, and even individuals who have had a child together. If you're facing domestic violence accusations, understanding these facts is crucial for building a strong defense.
